clauses.reason: The order commands "do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverage Wholesale Industry" under title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act for the Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverage Wholesale Industry; the approval has legal effect only through section 3 of that title (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed", so the prospective operative effect of this approval ended on June 14, 1935, the date of approval, because the resolution states no later effective date. The recital that the code was presented by the Secretary of Agriculture under section 3(d) does not change this: section 2 of the resolution repeals the provisions "delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes". No held record shows this code cancelled or suspended earlier, and the order states no own-terms end. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. The Schechter decision of May 27, 1935 is recorded only as a validity characterization, not an end date.

inventory_overrides.reason: Complete operative inventory corrected from the provisional APP text: findings 1 to 4 are recitals that precede the command, and the only operative provision is the final approval of the code; the span runs from the second "Now, Therefore" to the end of that sentence.

research_rationale:
The held American Presidency Project transcription of EO:6487A (signed December 9, 1933) recites that the Secretary of Agriculture submitted the code, finds that notice was given and hearings held "upon a code of fair competition presented by the Secretary of Agriculture upon his own motion pursuant to section 3 (d) of the act", that the code complies with clause (2) of section 3(a), and that it will tend to effectuate the policy of Congress, then ends with the only command, "do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverage Wholesale Industry". The findings are predicates, not commands. It states no period, condition, "until" date, exception or provisional approval, so no own-terms end applies. Section 3(d) of Title I let the President prescribe a code with the same effect as an approved code, so the command depends on section 3, and under the reviewed shared analysis its first end is the statutory repeal on June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 section 2, "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"; approved June 14, 1935), which reaches power "to approve or prescribe" codes, unless a held record shows an earlier cancellation or suspension, and none is held for this code.

Nothing in the held sources continues the approval itself after the repeal.
